moduleTitle: Automating Mobile Apps on TMA — Part 3: Dynamic Device Allocation
learningObjectives: Set the documented DeviceName value for Appium dynamic selection.
Distinguish dynamic selection from a fixed target identifier and arbitrary wildcard syntax.
Use documented platform and OS configuration for the chosen connection.
Validate the actual selected target and its application state.
Investigate device availability and test assumptions using execution evidence.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: From the concept to the configuration

elements.description: Tosca documents a DeviceName value that requests Appium dynamic selection of a connected Android or iOS device. This independent local guide explains that setting and operational checks; it does not reproduce an unavailable Academy exercise or certify a scheduling policy.

bulletPoints: A fixed target and dynamic selection have different target assumptions.

elements.description: Set DeviceName to TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION to request that Appium dynamically select a connected iOS or Android device. This is a documented literal value, not arbitrary wildcard syntax or a criterion expression. The guide does not establish a Ready/non-Busy scheduler, fairness, queue timing or reservation guarantee.

elements.title: Configuration to verify
items: In Mobile Scan’s Add device dialog, enter the dynamic-selection value in the device ID field, select Android or iOS, and specify Real or Simulated for iOS as appropriate.
The OSVersion TCP is documented for an iOS simulator and Android version-based selection without an exact ID. Use its documented version value; do not invent a minimum-version comparison syntax.
Check the chosen connection and driver’s supported capabilities. Scan configuration choices are not a universal farm-filter language for model, form factor or platform.

elements.text: Select a platform and supported configuration appropriate to the test. Inspect the resolved device and application state rather than assuming every connected target is interchangeable.

bulletPoints: Use the exact documented literal and connection configuration.
Validate actual target suitability; no arbitrary wildcard grammar is established.

elements.description: The documentation assigns dynamic selection to Appium. Do not infer that TMA implements a particular queue, filtering or reservation algorithm. Record the selected target from available execution/session evidence and validate the required application state.

elements.text: Avoid assuming that a dynamically selected target repeats a previous device’s display or installed state. Fixed targeting can make a device requirement explicit, but even a fixed device still needs availability and state checks.

bulletPoints: Appium selects the target; a repeated specific device is not promised.
Check application and layout assumptions against the observed target.

elements.title: Investigation hypotheses
items: If no usable target can be selected, inspect connected devices, effective configuration, driver errors and supported versions.
If the actual target differs from the one used to author the test, inspect unsupported layout or application-state assumptions.
For concurrent runs, compare requested sessions with confirmed available compatible devices. Both static and dynamic targeting can encounter an unavailable or occupied device.

elements.text: These are independent operational checks, not guaranteed diagnoses. Use logs and actual target/capability evidence to distinguish capacity, configuration, driver and application problems.

bulletPoints: Availability and contention are not exclusive to dynamic targeting.
Capacity changes help only when evidence identifies insufficient compatible devices.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming the same device resolves on every run
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A TestCase built and validated once against a dynamically-allocated device, with assumptions baked in about that specific device's screen size or pre-installed state.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Validate the selected target and application state. Use a fixed target when a particular device is required, while still checking its availability.

examPitfalls.title: Treating the selection literal as a filter expression
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Inventing platform/model wildcard syntax inside DeviceName.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION exactly. Configure only supported platform, OS and driver options for the chosen connection.

examPitfalls.title: Blaming a single TCP for intermittent dynamic-allocation failures
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming any timeout proves insufficient pool capacity.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Compare available compatible targets and concurrent demand alongside effective configuration and driver logs. Capacity is one hypothesis, not every timeout’s cause.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does setting DeviceName to TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION request?

options.text: A fixed udid pinned to one physical device.
Appium dynamic selection of a connected Android or iOS device.
The IP address of the TMA server.
A licence key scoped to a specific device.

practiceQuiz.hint: The documented literal requests target selection; it is not a wildcard expression.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Tosca device table assigns this value to Appium dynamic device selection. It is neither a fixed ID nor a server address or license key.

optionExplanations.A: A fixed ID selects a particular target instead of requesting dynamic selection.
optionExplanations.B: This is the documented meaning of the literal value.
optionExplanations.C: The server address is configured separately.
optionExplanations.D: DeviceName is not a license credential.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Execution evidence confirms a dynamically selected device has a different screen layout from the one assumed by the test, causing the failing control interaction. What explains this failure?

options.text: Dynamic allocation is fundamentally broken and should never be used.
The TestCase's device-specific assumptions don't hold on every device dynamic allocation might resolve to.
TMA has run out of licences.
The AVD needs to be recreated.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario establishes an actual layout mismatch.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The observed target does not satisfy the test’s layout assumptions. Support the required layouts or use an explicit compatible target; this evidence does not establish licensing or AVD corruption.

optionExplanations.A: The observed mismatch does not establish a platform-wide defect.
optionExplanations.B: The actual layout differs from the test’s confirmed assumptions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two concurrent tests need separate devices, but evidence confirms only one compatible device is currently available. Which investigation addresses that capacity gap?

options.text: Whether the pool has enough matching devices for the expected parallel load.
Whether the TMAServer TCP has a trailing slash.
Whether the app under test needs to be reinstalled.
Whether LiveView is enabled.

practiceQuiz.hint: The available device count is established by the scenario.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Compare available compatible devices with the requested concurrent sessions. The confirmed capacity gap warrants investigation; a generic timeout alone would not prove it.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario confirms insufficient compatible concurrent targets.
optionExplanations.B: URL formatting does not resolve this confirmed capacity gap.
optionExplanations.C: Reinstallation is not supported by the supplied evidence.
optionExplanations.D: LiveView screenshots do not add device capacity.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With suitable connected devices and validated test state, which are potential benefits of dynamic selection rather than pinning each test to one device? (three correct answers)

options.text: Flexibility in testing across devices
Potentially improved use of available compatible devices
Reduced need for pre-installed apps
Less per-test fixed-device configuration when a compatible setup grows

practiceQuiz.hint: These are possible operational benefits, not guaranteed throughput or provisioning.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Selecting from suitable connected targets can offer flexibility, better utilization and reduced fixed-target configuration. These benefits depend on compatible targets and test state; dynamic selection neither installs the app by itself nor guarantees scheduling throughput.

optionExplanations.A: Suitable dynamic targets can offer flexibility.
optionExplanations.B: Utilization may improve when compatible devices are available; this is not a scheduling guarantee.
optionExplanations.C: Dynamic selection does not provision an application.
optionExplanations.D: A compatible setup can grow without assigning each test a new fixed ID.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which documented DeviceName value requests Appium dynamic device selection?

options.text: TOSCA_STATIC_DEVICE_SELECTION
DYNAMIC_DEVICE_TARGETING
TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION
DEVICE_TARGET_DYNAMIC

practiceQuiz.rationale: TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION is the documented value. The other strings are not that value; fixed targeting uses the identifier/name required by the actual connection.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the documented dynamic value.
optionExplanations.C: This is the exact documented value.

quickRecap.value: Use the exact DeviceName literal TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION.
Appium selects a connected target; repeated identity and scheduling guarantees are not established.
Use documented platform/OS and driver configuration, not an invented wildcard grammar.
Availability, layout assumptions and contention require evidence; static targets also need availability.
Validate actual target and session evidence before choosing capacity or configuration remedies.
